label: Canonical Perturbation Theory
notes: Open by framing the chapter as the bridge between exactly solvable mechanics and the chaotic generic case. Integrable systems give invariant tori; perturbation theory asks whether those tori survive. The small denominator obstruction and the KAM rescue are the two poles of the whole story we develop today.

label: Integrable Systems
notes: State precisely what integrable means: n functionally independent integrals in involution on a 2n-dimensional symplectic manifold. Stress that involution, the vanishing Poisson bracket, is what makes the joint level sets into smooth invariant manifolds carrying commuting flows, not just intersecting hypersurfaces.

label: Liouville-Arnold Theorem
notes: Walk through the conclusion: a compact connected common level set of the integrals is diffeomorphic to an n-torus, and a neighborhood foliates into such tori. Emphasize that commuting complete vector fields on a compact manifold force the torus topology by the classification of such group actions.

label: Invariant Tori
notes: Make the torus concrete with the two action circles. Each independent integral fixes one radius; the angles run around the holes. The trajectory is a straight winding line on the flat torus, so visualizing the winding slope is the key intuition for everything about resonance that follows.

label: Action-Angle Variables
notes: Introduce action-angle coordinates as the canonical chart that trivializes integrable dynamics. Actions are adiabatic-style invariants built from loop integrals of the momentum one-form; angles are uniform coordinates. In these variables Hamilton's equations decouple completely and the Hamiltonian depends on actions alone.

label: Conditionally Periodic Motion
notes: Define conditionally periodic motion and tie it to the frequency vector, the gradient of the Hamiltonian in actions. Rational frequency ratios close into periodic orbits; irrational ratios fill the torus densely. This dichotomy is exactly what perturbation theory will have to respect torus by torus.

label: Nearly Integrable Systems
notes: Set up the perturbation problem with the split Hamiltonian. The unperturbed part depends only on actions; the small term reintroduces angle dependence. Our goal is a canonical change of variables removing the angle dependence to higher order, which is where the obstruction will surface immediately.

label: The Averaging Principle
notes: Present averaging as the leading approximation: replace the perturbation by its angle average so actions drift slowly while angles spin fast. Explain that this works cleanly away from resonance, and that the formal generating function involves dividing Fourier coefficients by frequency combinations.

label: Small Denominators
notes: Expose the core difficulty. The generating function carries terms divided by integer combinations of the frequencies, and these denominators come arbitrarily close to zero on resonant and near-resonant tori. Even with bounded numerators the series can diverge, so naive perturbation theory fails near resonances.

label: Diophantine Frequencies
notes: Explain the cure conceptually. Restrict to strongly non-resonant frequencies satisfying a Diophantine condition bounding the denominators from below. Such frequencies are typical in the measure sense, so most tori avoid the dangerous resonances even though resonant tori are dense.

label: The KAM Theorem
notes: State Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser carefully. For a non-degenerate integrable system and a sufficiently small perturbation, most invariant tori survive, merely deformed, with the same frequencies. The surviving set has large measure, and tori are lost in a thin neighborhood of the resonances.

label: Resonance and Recap
notes: Close with the global picture: surviving KAM tori interleaved with shrinking resonance zones where chaos nucleates. Recap the logical chain from integrability through action-angle variables and small denominators to the KAM survival result, and preview how growing perturbation erodes the tori.
